AUTHOR: Xu
TITLE: Underwater Fish Detection using Deep Learning for Water Power Applications
REGION: Fall of Warness, Scotland (tidal); Wells Dam, Washington, USA (river); Kvichak River, Igiugig, Alaska, USA (river)
SPECIES: Unknown fish (Voith Hydro); Chinook and Sockeye salmon (Wells Dam); adult and smolt salmon (Igiugig) — single 'fish' class
DATA: Own footage: three MHK/hydropower underwater video datasets (Voith Hydro 15,918 frames; Wells Dam 24,000; Igiugig 30,277), frame-wise annotated
V_EV: Sec. V: 'the real world environment pose new difficulties including light, turbidity, high flow speed'; Sec. IV.A: 'The water flows fast in this dataset, with air bubbles and debris'. Words only; no measurement; results stratified by dataset not by visibility.
D2: ~80/20 train/test per dataset; 10% of test set used for validation
D_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'For each of the three fish video datasets, we divided them into roughly 80% - 20% for training and testing.'
R_EV: Table III (Experiment II, trained on Voith Hydro and Wells Dam only): testing mAP 0.5714 (Voith Hydro) and 0.5659 (Wells Dam) versus 0.0055 on Igiugig ('# of training frame 0')
E_EV: Tables II–III: only testing mAP (0.5392 overall; 0.5474 / 0.5575 / 0.4507 per dataset) and precision-recall curves reported.
ARCH: YOLOv3 (Keras/TensorFlow fork of experiencor/keras-yolo3), Adam lr 1e-4, early stop at 20 epochs
METR: mAP; precision-recall curves; false positives / true positives counts output
NOTE: Split unit is ambiguous: text says only 'roughly 80%-20%' per dataset; a remark that 'the error continued for the entire testing video' and 'If we move the troublesome video to training set' hints at a video-level split, but it is never stated, so D1=NR (lower-information value). R1=Y: Experiment II holds out the whole Igiugig dataset (different site, camera, resolution, species) — external test with quantified failure (mAP 0.0055) followed by fine-tuning; R3=Y coded on that basis. C1=NR: predictions shown with confidence scores but no operating threshold reported; PR curves discussed as operating points but C_ALL P requires C1=Y, so C_ALL=NR. PRE=COCO inferred from use of official YOLOv3 weights and the Discussion's statement that 'The COCO dataset does not contain a fish object class, so the usefulness of the pre-trained weights used for this study is questionable'. Only frames with fish were used in training. ENV=혼합 (one tidal marine site, two river sites). Data and scripts public at github.com/wenweixu/keras-yolo3.
